label: late original steps / <DEL> in sequences starting with c (strongest on input y)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.003% of steps). About 91% of activations, and 91% of activation mass, fall in sequences whose first original token is c, at steps t = 6-9 in the original phase or at the <DEL> step. It mostly appears when L = 8-9, close to the end of the original phase (to_go 0-1). It never fires during the copy phase or at t < 5. Magnitude is largest when the input is y (58% of mass; the top example is c 3 k 2 r u u y, where y follows u). Earlier k or u tokens in the sequence are common in active examples, but they do not separate active from inactive steps. Precision is very poor: the context fires on less than 1% of matching steps, and adding in_tok == y only raises F1 to about 0.18, so what makes a given c-initial sequence trigger the feature is still unexplained. It is not a pure token detector: y on its own, or c on its own, is far from sufficient.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=c (+4.92), prev_tok=u (+2.61), orig2=k (+2.47), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=y (+2.14), phase=0 & in_tok=y (+2.14), orig3=p (+2.06). Lower it: next_out=- (-2.51), phase=2 (-2.01), in_first=0 (-1.69), orig7=- (-1.60).
